title: OAB Reasoning Trace
description: The auditable chain behind one architectural decision: inputs, assumptions, knowledge consulted, options weighed, the choice, and the conditions that would reverse it. This is what lets a developer disagree with a specific link rather than accept or reject a conclusion whole.

decision.description: What is being decided, e.g. 'Primary datastore'.

stage.description: Maturity stage of the system. Filters knowledge retrieval, so stage-4 machinery cannot be offered to a stage-1 system.

mitigation.description: What is being dropped, who will operate the excess, or which engineer is being hired. An override without one of these is a wish.

override.description: Required when spent exceeds available. Going over budget is allowed; going over silently is not.

assumptions.description: Never empty and never hidden. A user who can see the assumptions can correct the input instead of distrusting the tool.

impact.description: How much the answer moves if this is wrong.

knowledge_used.description: Ids of the knowledge units consulted, so the reasoning can be traced back to its sources.

options.description: At least two, and one of them must be the simplest viable option — stated fairly, not as a straw man. Most architecture failure is failing to consider 'just use the database you already have'.

reversibility.description: A reversible decision made quickly usually beats a perfect decision made slowly. One-way doors deserve more analysis.

reason.description: For a rejected option, the measurement that would change the answer — not merely why it lost.

trade_offs.description: Never empty for the selected option. An option with no downsides has not been understood.

triggers.description: Ids of the evolution triggers that would reopen this decision.

then.description: A trace with a selection must also record a rejection. If nothing was rejected, no alternative was genuinely considered.
